mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent economic strength indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7%, the combination signals a highly accommodative monetary policy in a weak labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with high unemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent market strength.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent consumer demand strength indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 jobs in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decline does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) is growing and retail sales (RSAFS) are declining, it signals a mismatch between production and consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of GDPC1 growth with RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent market weakness.
